title: PRESS RELEASE (DRAFT) — Redwood Inference releases Latency-per-Dollar Benchmark Report for Production LLM Serving

====================
PRESS RELEASE (DRAFT)
====================
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE (under embargo until [DATE/TIME])

Headline:
Redwood Inference Publishes “Latency per Dollar” Benchmark Report to Help Teams Optimize Production LLM Serving

Subheadline:
New report measures real-world inference economics across leading open models and multiple cloud regions, with a reproducible methodology designed for engineering teams

Dateline:
SAN FRANCISCO — [MONTH] [DATE], 2025

Body:
Redwood Inference, a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, today announced the release of its new Latency-per-Dollar Benchmark Report. The report is designed to help engineering teams evaluate the true production economics of LLM serving—balancing latency, throughput, and cost—across popular open models and cloud regions.

As LLM use expands from prototypes to revenue-critical applications, teams are discovering that model selection is only part of the equation. Serving performance and operational reliability—especially the cost of meeting latency targets at scale—often determines whether an LLM feature can be shipped sustainably.

“Latency per dollar is the metric teams end up backing into when they go from demos to production,” said [CRO NAME], Chief Revenue Officer at Redwood Inference. “This report gives builders a clear, defensible way to reason about unit economics across model families and regions—and a starting point to replicate the approach on their own workloads.”

The Latency-per-Dollar Benchmark Report includes:
- Coverage across multiple model families and cloud regions (North America, Europe, and at least one APAC region)
- Workload definitions spanning chat and embeddings baselines
- Summary results with supporting throughput and cost metrics
- A methodology appendix describing concurrency settings, warmup policy, caching/batching rules, and variance handling

“Most benchmark discussions stop at raw speed or headline price,” said Camila Reyes, VP of Marketing at Redwood Inference. “Production teams need to know how performance and cost trade off under realistic concurrency and traffic patterns. We built this report to be useful to engineers and credible to procurement—without hiding the constraints.”

Methodology and reproducibility
The report’s methodology was developed and validated by Redwood’s Applied ML and performance evaluation teams. It emphasizes repeatability, explicit measurement windows, and clear guidance on interpreting variance.

“Our goal was to publish something other engineering teams can audit and reproduce,” said Jonas Weber, VP of Applied ML at Redwood Inference. “We document the workload distributions, the settings that materially affect results, and the rerun policy when variance exceeds thresholds. Benchmarks are only useful when the assumptions are visible.”

[Optional paragraph if we want to highlight the platform tie-in—keep non-claimy]
Redwood Inference customers can use Redwood’s Console and optimization tooling to observe token-level latency and cost drivers, apply caching and batching policies, and deploy consistent inference across hosted, dedicated capacity, or private environments.
